edges.description: RIM-binding proteins tie voltage-gated calcium channels to release-ready vesicles, so their loss is expected to make action-potential-evoked release slower and less reliable.
edges.target: Impaired Coupling of Calcium Influx to Synaptic Vesicle Release

edges.description: Complete loss of RIMBP1 in mice reduces Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and cerebellar synapse number.
edges.target: Cerebellar Purkinje Cell Dendritic and Synaptic Deficit

edges.description: Biallelic loss-of-function TSPOAP1 variants are associated with intellectual disability alongside juvenile-onset generalized dystonia through unresolved neural circuit mechanisms.

Biallelic loss-of-function TSPOAP1 variants are associated with cerebellar atrophy in human patients; whether this directly reflects the mouse Purkinje cell dendritic and synaptic deficit remains unresolved.
Truncating TSPOAP1 variants are associated with eye movement abnormalities through unresolved oculomotor circuit mechanisms.
The authors conclude that presynaptic active-zone dysfunction causes the dystonia; the circuit through which it acts is not identified.

edges.description: The knockout is the source of the cerebellar cellular node; whether patients have the same Purkinje dendritic and synaptic deficit is unknown.
edges.limitations: The mouse shows motor abnormalities described only as reminiscent of dystonia, and the human cerebellar findings are MRI atrophy rather than histology, so correspondence between the mouse cellular deficit and the human phenotype is assumed rather than shown.

nodes.description: Homozygous truncating TSPOAP1 variants (a frameshift and a nonsense variant in the original families; further truncating variants in later reports) are predicted to abolish RIMBP1, an active-zone protein of the presynaptic release machinery. Loss of RIMBP1 protein has not been measured in patient neurons; the loss-of-function reading rests on variant class and on the knockout mouse.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic variants in TSPOAP1, encoding the active-zone protein RIMBP1, cause autosomal recessive dystonia.
evidence.snippet: Subjects carrying loss-of-function variants presented with juvenile-onset progressive generalized dystonia, associated with intellectual disability and cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.snippet: We describe two unrelated patients with adolescent-onset generalized dystonia showing cranio-caudal progression due to novel truncating variants in the TSPOAP1 gene.

evidence.snippet: RIM-binding proteins (RIM-BPs) are multidomain active zone proteins that bind to RIMs and to Ca(2+) channels.

molecular_functions: RIM and voltage-gated calcium channel adaptor activity

nodes.description: Tspoap1-knockout mice show reduced Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and fewer cerebellar synapses. This is a mouse cellular finding. It is not linked here to patient cerebellar atrophy or to dystonia by an edge, because the source does not show that the cerebellar change causes either; nor is this node conformed to the cerebellar Purkinje degeneration module, since Purkinje neuron loss and cerebellar ataxia are not what the source reports.

nodes.description: Without RIM-binding proteins, release is not abolished but becomes slower and less reliable because calcium channels are not held close to primed vesicles. The single-protein (RIMBP1-only) effect and its magnitude in human motor circuits are inferred, and which neuronal population carries the defect that produces dystonia is unknown.
